minutes.headline: Task force heard plans to add controls to school mini-splits for a fall grant round; no formal votes except adjournment.
minutes.summary: The Green Community committee met with school officials about phase two of the mini-split project at the primary school, including integrating controls with the building system and a utility rebate for phase one. They discussed Turkey Hill heating and cooling problems, weatherization, and street light savings. A joint meeting with the schools was planned, a member said he is moving out of state, and the meeting adjourned.

budget_items.topic: Unitil rebate for phase one mini-splits
budget_items.what_was_said: Unitil told the committee a per-head-unit rebate could recoup some phase one costs for six condensing units.
Pucks for each of 12 rooms were estimated at about a hundred dollars each; installation labor/IT approach undecided.

budget_items.topic: Phase two units and utility incentive
budget_items.what_was_said: Sixteen spaces with no units would need roughly eight head units, with an estimated Unitil incentive; the grant allocation was recalled as a larger number.
Walk-in refrigeration controls for schools total a small amount with a short payback; to be considered alongside extra mini-splits.
The sewer pump station project had a very long payback and was judged not worth including in the application.

budget_items.topic: Street light bills, Lunenburg vs Fitchburg
budget_items.what_was_said: Lunenburg's LED street light bill was far lower than Fitchburg's, with dimming credited for savings.

budget_items.topic: Final application: cruisers, training, and mini-split award
budget_items.what_was_said: Possible funds for police cruisers were discussed along with whether adding them would affect the mini-split award; training is funded separately by Unitil.
A member said spending on building reuse iterations has reached several hundred thousand dollars.

decisions.decision: Walk-through of primary school systems set for September 20 with Unitil, the controls vendor, and the town; school IT manager to attend.
Agreed to post a joint meeting with the school department on the mini-split project for September 26 at 7:30 a.m.
Sewer pump station projects will not be included in the grant application because of the long payback.
August minutes could not be reviewed (file lost); to be redone and both sets reviewed at the next meeting.
Chair to send a notice to poll members for a next meeting the week of September 30.

what_happened.line: Task force members heard school officials describe a second phase of mini-split heat pumps at the primary school, to be paired with building controls, for a fall grant application.
Utility staff said a per-unit rebate could recoup part of the first phase's cost; no vote was taken on any grant item.
Sewer pump station projects were dropped from the grant application because of their long payback.
A joint meeting with the school department on the mini-split project was agreed for September 26 at 7:30 a.m., and a building walk-through was set for September 20.
August minutes could not be reviewed because the file was lost; they are to be redone and both sets reviewed next meeting. The only vote was to adjourn.

why_it_matters: The fall Green Communities grant application decides which energy projects at the primary school get state money, which affects how much heating and cooling work the town funds on its own.
Nothing was voted on, so the scope of the application, including whether police cruisers are added and how that interacts with the mini-split award, remains open for the next meetings.
